title: Building in the Gemini Era – Kat Kampf & Ammaar Reshi, Google DeepMind

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 87%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on Google AI Studio as a developer platform for vibe coding, with upcoming full-stack runtime support abstracting backend complexity for builders. AI Studio is a developer platform for building AI-powered applications, while the comic and sticker demos showcase media-creative content generation. The demos focus on development and rapid prototyping of applications through natural-language prompting in AI Studio. The session emphasizes democratizing software creation for non-engineers and beginners through vibe coding. Multiple live demos are presented including comic generation, sticker creation, shader websites, UI cloning, and a multiplayer racing game. All claims are sourced from statements made in the transcript with corresponding evidence anchors.

summary: Kat Kampf and Ammaar Reshi of Google DeepMind introduce two newly launched models: Gemini 3 Pro and Nano Banana Pro. Gemini 3 Pro is positioned as their most intelligent state-of-the-art model with two major capabilities: strong UI and aesthetic sensibilities for one-shot website generation, and superior agentic tool calling for complex tasks within large codebases. A SWE-bench experiment shows Gemini 3 vastly outperforming other models in agentic scenarios. Nano Banana Pro represents a leap in image generation with Google Search-powered world knowledge, improved text rendering across multiple languages, consistency supporting up to 14 people in group shots, creative controls like focus shifting, and multiple aspect ratios. The speakers demonstrate vibe coding in Google AI Studio, a free-to-use build experience where users can prompt applications into existence using AI chips for features like Google Search grounding, Google Maps grounding, and the Live API. Demos include a comic book generator, a laptop sticker generator using search grounding, and a shader-animated website. They also show using AI Studio to ideate on its own features, cloning the AI Studio UI and adding an export flow to the newly announced Anti-Gravity IDE. Ammaar demos a 3D racing game built with simple prompts in Three.js, then attempts a live multiplayer version with the audience, reaching over 20 concurrent players. They tease upcoming full-stack runtime support in AI Studio, which will abstract away backend details like Express, databases, and payment solutions, letting users simply request features like multiplayer. Kat emphasizes the broader mission: democratizing software creation so anyone can build applications, and rethinking paradigms to infer user intent rather than forcing users to specify technical details.

sections.title: Intro & Gemini 3 Overview
sections.summary: Kat Kampf introduces herself and Ammaar Reshi, discussing Google DeepMind's long innovation history from transformers to AlphaGo. They announce Gemini 3 Pro as their latest state-of-the-art model with two key capabilities: one-shot UI design with strong aesthetic sensibilities, and agentic tool calling for complex codebase tasks. A SWE-bench experiment shows Gemini 3 vastly outperforming other models in agentic scenarios.

sections.title: Nano Banana Pro Capabilities
sections.summary: Ammaar Reshi introduces Nano Banana Pro, highlighting its Google Search-powered world knowledge for accurate infographics, improved text rendering that wraps around objects, localization in multiple languages like Korean, consistency supporting up to 14 people in group shots, creative controls like focus shifting, and multiple aspect ratios for different use cases.

sections.title: Vibe Coding in AI Studio
sections.summary: Kat demonstrates Google AI Studio's vibe coding experience, showing a gallery of example apps and the prompt-to-apply feature. She highlights AI chips for integrating Gemini API features like Google Search grounding, Google Maps grounding, and Live API. The platform is free to use, and shared apps use visitors' free quota to avoid surprise API bills.

sections.title: Comic Book Demo: Text Rendering & Consistency
sections.summary: Ammaar demos a comic book generator app that uploads faces, selects genre and language, and creates personalized stories. He also shows a shader-animated website built from a simple prompt. The comic book demo showcases Nano Banana Pro's text rendering and Gemini 3's creative storytelling, including interactive story direction choices. The stories are genuinely humorous, a first for such models.

sections.title: Laptop Stickers Demo: Search Grounding
sections.summary: Kat demonstrates a laptop sticker generator using Google Search grounding with the Nano Banana Pro model. Users can enter words or use Google Search to generate personalized stickers. The demo searches for information about Ammaar to create contextually relevant stickers. Nano Banana Pro is currently a page experience in AI Studio requiring an API key, with selectable resolution options.

sections.title: "Anti-Gravity" & Ideating AI Studio Features
sections.summary: Kat shows how they use AI Studio to ideate on AI Studio features, demonstrating a one-shot prompt that clones the AI Studio UI from a screenshot and adds an export-to-Anti-Gravity-IDE button. Google announced the Anti-Gravity agentic IDE earlier in the week. The demo highlights how vibe coding tools can explore creative UI ideas outside existing patterns, with the model sometimes generating different export interfaces like a command line.

sections.title: 3D Racing Game & Full Stack Runtime
sections.summary: Ammaar demos a 3D racing game built in Three.js from simple prompts, featuring a bot opponent and a boost cheat. He teases upcoming full-stack runtime support in AI Studio that will abstract away backend details like Express, databases, and payment solutions, letting users simply request features like multiplayer without technical knowledge.

sections.title: Live Multiplayer Demo Attempt
sections.summary: Kat and Ammaar attempt a live multiplayer racing game with the audience via QR code. Over 20 players join, but the race struggles to start as not everyone hits ready. Collisions between cars cause bouncing. Despite the chaos, the runtime does not crash, demonstrating the potential of multiplayer vibe-coded apps.

sections.title: Democratizing Software & Closing Thoughts
sections.summary: Kat and Ammaar emphasize the broader mission of democratizing software creation, citing a tech support person who started vibe coding after watching a YouTube video. They discuss rethinking paradigms to infer user intent rather than forcing technical specifications, with full-stack runtime handling storage, payments, and other backend needs automatically. They invite the audience to share examples and questions via Twitter.
